output.brief: Resignations are concentrated in the Kestrel team: 8 of 11 Kestrel associates left, against 1 of 13 other associates in the group. Other groups look normal, so general market mobility and the firm-wide hours target are unlikely explanations. Pay is also a weak explanation: it applies to the whole group, yet almost nobody outside Kestrel left. The records cannot separate two explanations. Every Kestrel associate reports to Dorian Faulk, and Faulk supervises nobody else. So heavy workload and his supervision are completely confounded. Survey comments mention both weekend workload and humiliating late-night corrections. Faulk's own March email admits the team is understaffed and he is keeping people late. I'm fairly sure the problem is specific to Kestrel. I'm not sure whether workload or supervision is the main cause. Don't announce the retention payment or close the review. It would cost about £228k, probably miss the cause, and shut down inquiry. Next, commission the roughly £9k confidential external interviews, structured to separate supervision from workload. Meanwhile, consider interim relief on Kestrel staffing, and start tracking matter and supervising partner in attrition reporting. Document review ends in December, so timing matters.
